Alright, let me think this through. I'll stay in character as the farmer.

---

**My reasoning (老李, 59岁, 种了40年地)**

I've been farming this 7 mu for most of my life. University degree — I went to agricultural college back in the late 1980s — so I think about my fields a little more systematically than my neighbors, but 7 mu is still 7 mu. I can't afford to waste inputs, and I can't afford a crop failure either. With two kids working in the city and sending some money back, plus my wife's small shop income, I have a bit more cushion than the pure smallholders around me, but farming is still serious money for this household.

**Winter wheat** — already in the ground since October 15th last year. I used Jimai-22, the variety that's done well in my plots for about six years now. I put down 40 kg of 15-15-15 compound as base at sowing — that gives me 6 kg N, 6 kg P₂O₅, and 6 kg K₂O per mu as the foundation. Right now in late April we're at jointing, which is exactly when I need to topdress. I'm going out this week with about 25 kg of urea per mu, watered in with my first spring irrigation. That puts me at ~18 kg N/mu total — I target 500 kg/mu yield and the formula I use is roughly 30-35 kg N per 1000 kg grain, accounting for soil supply. I'll irrigate again at heading around mid-May, and if grain fill looks stressed in late May I'll do one more. That's winter + 3 spring irrigations — four total for wheat. Herbicide went down in late March (tribenuron-methyl for broadleaves). No fungicide planned unless I see stripe rust at flag leaf. Harvest around June 8-12 with the contracted combine.

**Summer maize** — goes in within 3 days of the wheat combine leaving the field. That turnaround is the tightest window of the year; 40 years of doing this and it still makes me nervous. I'll direct-drill Zhengdan-958 with the no-till planter (I rent the neighbor's) — 4 kg seed per mu, plus a starter fertilizer band of 30 kg compound 18-12-15. Then I topdress 20 kg urea at V8 (big trumpet stage, around late July). Total N about 16 kg/mu, which is lower than wheat because maize pulls from the residual wheat N and the summer rains help. I plan on 1 irrigation at silking (early August) — if the July rains come through I may skip it, that's 50 yuan/mu saved per application and the well costs add up. Atrazine+acetochlor mix at planting for weeds, and I'll scout for armyworm and stem borer in July.

I'm not changing much this year. Grain prices are okay, fertilizer costs are similar to last year. The main thing is watching the weather at grain fill and silking — those are the windows that make or break my yield. Total cash input about 6,300 yuan across both crops. My wife and I handle almost all the labor ourselves; the combine and planter are the only hired machinery.
